# Static image export

[`save_image()`](https://msummersgill.github.io/plotly.R.core/reference/save_image.md)
exports a figure with plotly.js’s own image export, running in a
headless Chromium-based browser driven by
[chromote](https://rstudio.github.io/chromote/). No Python, Kaleido or
orca is involved.

``` r

fig <- go_figure()
for (species in split(iris, iris$Species)) {
  fig <- add_scatter(
    fig, data = species, x = ~Sepal.Width, y = ~Sepal.Length,
    mode = "markers", name = as.character(species$Species[1])
  )
}
png_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
save_image(fig, png_file, width = 700, height = 450, scale = 2)
```

![Exported
figure](data:image/png;base64,)

## Formats and options

| Extension | Notes |
|----|----|
| `.png`, `.jpeg`/`.jpg`, `.webp` | `scale` multiplies the resolution (`scale = 2` for high-DPI) |
| `.svg` | WebGL traces (`scattergl`, 3D, maps) are embedded as images |
| `.pdf` | the SVG printed to a page the figure’s size |
| `.eps` | converted from the SVG; needs the rsvg package |

- `width`, `height`: pixels; default to the figure’s layout size, else
  700 × 500.
- LaTeX
  ([`TeX()`](https://msummersgill.github.io/plotly.R.core/reference/TeX.md))
  is typeset with the MathJax bundled with plotly.core, so it works
  offline.
- The browser starts on the first export (about a second) and is reused
  for the rest of the session.
  [`chrome_exporter()`](https://msummersgill.github.io/plotly.R.core/reference/save_image.md)
  gives a browser of your own, with `$transform(p, file, ...)` and
  `$shutdown()`.

## Setup

Requirements: chromote ≥ 0.5.0 (`install.packages("chromote")`), rsvg
for EPS only, and a Chromium-based browser. The browser is not an R
package, but on most machines it needs no separate install:
[`save_image()`](https://msummersgill.github.io/plotly.R.core/reference/save_image.md)
uses the first of

1.  the browser in the `CHROMOTE_CHROME` environment variable;
2.  an installed Google Chrome;
3.  an installed Microsoft Edge (on every Windows 10/11 machine),
    Chromium or Brave, including per-user installs;
4.  a Chrome Headless Shell downloaded earlier.

If there is none, it can download Chrome Headless Shell (about 125 MB)
from within R, into the user cache, without administrator rights. On
Linux it also downloads any shared libraries the browser lacks: the
packages providing them come from the system’s own repositories
(`apt-get download`, `dnf download`; Debian/Ubuntu and RHEL-family
systems) and are unpacked into
`tools::R_user_dir("plotly.core", "cache")`, not installed system-wide.

| Session | What happens |
|----|----|
| Interactive | One yes/no question, then [`install_chrome()`](https://msummersgill.github.io/plotly.R.core/reference/install_chrome.md) runs and the export continues |
| Script, scheduled job, CI | No download; an error says to run [`plotly.core::install_chrome()`](https://msummersgill.github.io/plotly.R.core/reference/install_chrome.md) once (e.g. in a setup script or Dockerfile) |
| R Markdown / Quarto | Never downloads; without a browser, figures are included as widgets |

[`remove_chrome()`](https://msummersgill.github.io/plotly.R.core/reference/install_chrome.md)
deletes plotly.core’s downloads; `remove_chrome(browser = TRUE)` also
removes chromote’s Chrome Headless Shell.

### Linux servers

With administrator rights, the libraries can instead be installed
system-wide (the error message shows the command for the system):

``` sh
# Debian, Ubuntu
sudo apt-get install -y libnss3 libnspr4 libatk1.0-0 libatk-bridge2.0-0 libcups2 libdrm2 \
  libgbm1 libxkbcommon0 libxcomposite1 libxdamage1 libxfixes3 libxrandr2 libpango-1.0-0 \
  libcairo2 libasound2
# RHEL, Rocky, AlmaLinux, Fedora, Amazon Linux
sudo dnf install -y nss nspr atk at-spi2-atk cups-libs libdrm mesa-libgbm libxkbcommon \
  libXcomposite libXdamage libXfixes libXrandr pango cairo alsa-lib
```

- Running as root (common in containers): Chrome needs `--no-sandbox`,
  which chromote adds itself in Docker and CI; elsewhere use
  `chromote::set_chrome_args(c(chromote::get_chrome_args(), "--no-sandbox"))`.
  Small `/dev/shm`: add `"--disable-dev-shm-usage"` the same way.
- Text is drawn with the fonts Chrome finds; minimal images may need
  fonts installed to match desktop output.

### Where set-up from R isn’t enough

| Situation | What to do |
|----|----|
| No internet, proxy, or blocked downloads (storage.googleapis.com) | Set R’s proxy (`https_proxy`), or copy a browser in and set `CHROMOTE_CHROME` |
| Linux on ARM64 (no Chrome Headless Shell build) | Install the distribution’s Chromium package |
| Old OS (e.g. CentOS/RHEL 7, Windows before 10) | Current Chrome can’t run there; use a newer system |
| Linux without package lists (slim images), SUSE, Arch | Install the libraries, or Chromium, with the package manager |
| Alpine | `apk add chromium`, `CHROMOTE_CHROME=/usr/bin/chromium-browser` |
| Locked-down machines (AppLocker/WDAC, MDM, antivirus), `noexec` home | Use an approved installed Chrome or Edge |
| webR / Shinylive | Not possible: R can’t start other programs there |
| Hosted R (Posit Connect, shinyapps.io) | Install a browser in the image, or run [`install_chrome()`](https://msummersgill.github.io/plotly.R.core/reference/install_chrome.md) at deployment |

## Performance compared with Kaleido

Kaleido (the plotly R package’s
[`save_image()`](https://msummersgill.github.io/plotly.R.core/reference/save_image.md))
also drives Chrome, and can keep it running between exports. The
difference is the data path: the figure goes from R to JSON text, is
parsed into Python objects by reticulate, then serialized again by
Kaleido and sent to Chrome as JSON numbers. plotly.core sends it
straight from R to Chrome, with numeric arrays as base64 typed arrays,
which are smaller and much quicker to write and to read.

| Figure (700 × 500 PNG) | Kaleido 1.5 (s) | plotly.core (s) | Faster |
|:-----------------------|----------------:|----------------:|:-------|
| Scatter, 150 points    |           0.065 |           0.024 | 2.7×   |
| Line, 100,000 points   |           1.508 |           0.138 | 10.9×  |
| Line, 1,000,000 points |          13.033 |           0.767 | 17.0×  |
| Heatmap, 500 × 500     |           0.565 |           0.168 | 3.4×   |
| Heatmap, 1000 × 1000   |           2.002 |           0.557 | 3.6×   |

Seconds per export, median of 5, with both browsers already running
(`kaleido.start_sync_server()` for Kaleido), the same plotly.js 4.3.0
and Chrome 157, and matching images. Kaleido’s time includes writing the
figure’s JSON in R (0.86 s at 1M points; plotly.core’s typed-array JSON
takes 0.13 s) and parsing it in Python (0.16 s). Apple M3 Pro, macOS
26.5.1, 2026-11-16. Starting either browser adds about 1.3 s to the
first export.

Set-up compared:

|  | orca | Kaleido | plotly.core |
|----|----|----|----|
| Install | separate command-line app (npm/installer) | Python + `kaleido`, `plotly` via reticulate | `install.packages("chromote")` |
| Browser | bundled (Electron) | Chrome, installed separately (Kaleido 1.x) | installed Chrome/Edge/Chromium/Brave, or downloaded from R |

## Troubleshooting

| Message | Fix |
|----|----|
| needs chromote 0.5.0 or later | `install.packages("chromote")` |
| needs Chrome, which wasn’t found | [`plotly.core::install_chrome()`](https://msummersgill.github.io/plotly.R.core/reference/install_chrome.md), or set `CHROMOTE_CHROME` |
| shared libraries it needs are missing | [`plotly.core::install_chrome()`](https://msummersgill.github.io/plotly.R.core/reference/install_chrome.md), or the `sudo` command shown |
| Chrome … failed to start | Read Chrome’s output in the message; see [Linux servers](#linux-servers) |
| EPS export needs the rsvg package | `install.packages("rsvg")` |
